clues: A property of body fluids measured in mOsm/kg
It tells you how concentrated a solution is, based on the number of dissolved particles
Plasma normally has about 285 of these units per kilogram of water; sodium is the main contributor
An electrolyte disorder that can stop the heart
Serum level of a major intracellular ion is too high, often in renal failure
Causes tall peaked T waves on ECG and is treated first with IV calcium gluconate
A common clinical sign seen in the legs of some patients
Excess fluid collects in the tissue spaces outside the blood vessels
Pressing the skin leaves a pit; seen in heart failure, nephrotic syndrome and liver disease
